name: Adon Agro Commodities Limited
summary: Rapid growth into nut processing has not yet converted into dependable owner cash. FY2026 revenue ₹324.10 crore and PAT ₹23.17 crore coexist with CFO −₹9.04 crore, a large inventory/vendor-advance build and almost all reported bank balances tied to guarantees or overdraft collateral. BQS 4.26 and Growth Quality GQS 5.00 after the persistent-cash cap. At the dated secondary ₹96.70 quote, the conditional base model returns 16.51%, only 1.51 percentage points above a 15% hurdle; severe stress is unfunded. IAS remains NS because current BSE implementation restrictions are unverified. This is a speculative cash-conversion watchlist, not a high-quality compounder or an implementation recommendation.
identity_note: The issuer prospectus, annual report, AGM record and official security master match the ISIN; the issuer reports listing on 6 July 2026.

quote.kind: secondary historical close, not executable bid

score_note: BQS 4.26; raw Growth Quality 5.60 is capped at 5 for persistent CASH 1. R 6 is conditional on the model. L is NS, so IAS is NS, with unreweighted bounds of 4.065–4.965.

GOV.reason: Unmodified audit/IFC and trail reporting are positives, but connected trades, historic director-pay intensity, subsidiary wording and unresolved customs matter justify a cautious score. No diversion/conviction established.

MOAT.reason: Processing/service value exists, but concentrated sourcing and uncontracted commodity trade lack demonstrated durable pricing power. New brand is not an established franchise.

REV.reason: Three-full-year revenue CAGR is 143.91%; the short history, changed operating mix and Medium confidence impose a cap of 8. The FY22 stub is excluded.

DUR.reason: Processing and broader customers provide runway, but repeat demand, margin durability, clearance and working-capital funding remain fragile.

CAP.reason: Historical incremental NOPAT/capital of 36–39% is attractive but highly sensitive to the low base, margin transition and customer funding; cash evidence limits confidence in durability.

CASH.reason: FY24–26 CFO/PAT is −0.1873. FY26 inventory and vendor advances absorb cash despite customer advances. Restricted FDs are not distributable. Persistent weakness caps GQS at 5.

BAL.reason: Net IPO proceeds of ₹38.4427 crore improve funding after March, but March debt of ₹24.2838 crore, restricted cash, a ₹7.9616 crore tax provision and operating advances preclude a strong-balance-sheet claim.

EXEC.reason: Processing commenced and sales expanded, but the new plant has a short output history, the published dates-utilization arithmetic is inconsistent, and cash conversion is not proven.

EARN.reason: Core FY26 PAT of ₹22.54–22.58 crore after excluding other income remains reported profit, but stock build, uneven final two months and differences in restatement/EPS bases reduce confidence.

Q.reason: BQS weighted business quality, not an analyst override.

R.reason: Funded base IRR of 16.5132% less the 15% hurdle equals 1.5132 percentage points, in the 0–2 point bucket. The base case is funded without the IDBI line; reserving an additional ₹10 crore of IPO cash gives 16.04%. This is a forecast, not a guarantee.

D.reason: Documented leverage, advances and customs exposure support a severe unfunded path with a ₹45.27 crore gap; no rescue or precise liquidation recovery is assumed.

P.reason: Volatile commodity/FX working capital and uncertainty over the customs case and brand execution reduce probability confidence despite profitable growth and IPO equity.

L.reason: Historical price-volume bounds imply a starting capacity band of 9, below two sessions at 5% participation. The 2,000-share lot costs ₹193,400, and latest-day turnover of one lot warrants execution downgrades. Official MII decoding resolves SM eligibility and the 20% band; the ST duplicate is dormant. However, a dated secondary discovery reports BSE ST-ASM Stage I on 13 September, and current stage/removal is unverified. This potentially material restriction gap leaves L unscored, not merely the lack of a live spread.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Adon Agro Commodities Limited, BSE SME 544809, symbol ADON, ISIN INE1SME01017. Cutoff 20 October 2026. Listed 6 July 2026; fresh IPO of 6,290,000 shares at ₹70, no OFS, takes shares from 16,727,270 to 23,017,270. The official security master and September 28 AGM denominator agree. Market value at secondary 19 October close ₹96.70 is ₹222.5770 crore; one 2000-share lot costs ₹193,400. Five annual forward steps, 15% nominal equity hurdle, ₹5 lakh liquidity reference, before investor taxes. Scope is Indian GAAP Accounting Standards standalone, not Ind AS or a reconstructed consolidated group. Annual directors report says the Dubai subsidiary had no operations and no consolidated accounts were prepared, while a financial note says no subsidiary existed at reporting date; this inconsistency remains open. G1 Integrity / G2 Reliability: Conditional for reporting/connected-party/customs matters; G3 Funding: Conditional on collection and actual financing use, not observed default; G4 Tradability: Hold — unresolved. Original CSV date is unknown and supplies no verified current metric. The master’s epoch-decoded listing date is 7 July, one day later than the issuer’s repeated 6 July statement; the issuer date is retained with that discrepancy disclosed. Both precede the full 60-session observation window.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: Nine canonical business factors: GOV 4, MOAT 3, REV 8, DUR 4, CAP 5, CASH 1, BAL 5, EXEC 5, EARN 5. BQS = .20×4+.20×3+.12×8+.10×4+.12×5+.10×1+.08×5+.08×5=4.26. Growth Quality = .40×8+.20×4+.15×5+.15×5+.10×1=5.60, capped 5.00 for persistent weak cash conversion. REV uses three comparable full-year intervals, not the two-month incorporation stub, and is capped 8 despite 143.91% CAGR. Q 4.26, R 6, D 2, P 4, L NS. Known IAS contribution 3.965, missing L weight 0.10 yields 4.065–4.965 bounds; no renormalized IAS or implementation ranking. Forecast uncertainty is high even where source/input confidence is Medium.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: Adon imports, trades, processes and distributes dry fruits, nuts, seeds and berries. It began processing in July 2025 and moved to a new plant later that year, so FY2026 mixes a changed operating model with the earlier wholesaler. Annual domestic product sales ₹311.0013 crore, export sales ₹12.9216 crore and service income ₹0.177 crore approximately reconcile operating revenue ₹324.10 crore. Purchases/raw materials, import duty, logistics and working capital dominate economics. The ten-month prospectus direct-cost schedule includes ₹54.6166 crore customs duty and ₹7.1592 crore import-related charges; annual direct expenses ₹77.7748 crore are not all purchases of finished goods. Imported inventory is exposed to FX, food quality, clearance, spoilage and commodity prices. HungerNuts launches and Chile sourcing can extend distribution but do not yet demonstrate consumer pricing power. The September office/research lease adds cash cost and a two-year lock-in.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: MOAT 3: sourcing relationships, processing execution and a broader customer list can create service value, but no demonstrated patented process, scarce licensed franchise or long-duration contracted pricing advantage was found. Top-ten customer concentration falls from 92.78% in FY23 and 99.92% in FY24 to 58.75% in FY25 and 44.17% in the ten months to January 2026; customer counts 22/14/101/871 suggest diversification, but are not retention cohorts or commitments. FY25 five suppliers accounted for all purchases; the later top-ten share 50.21% improves but does not eliminate supply dependence. Plant capacity is not a moat by itself. The prospectus visually reports 11.7 tonnes of dates in two months against 1000 tonnes annual capacity and 70.20% utilization; simple annualization gives 7.02%, so the published 70.20% is not used as a verified utilization input. Walnuts 240.45 tonnes over two months against 2000 annual implies 72.14%; new almond capacity 4800 annual lacks comparable realized output in that table.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Restated FY23/24/25 operating revenue ₹22.3348/₹72.5671/₹103.0355 crore and FY26 annual ₹324.10 crore imply three-year CAGR 143.91%. The original FY22 revenue ₹1.9393 crore covers only 24 January–31 March after incorporation and is excluded from annualized growth scoring. There is no five-year operating history before incorporation to invent. Gross sales growth combines trading, processing, customer expansion and commodity/FX effects; a constant-volume organic bridge is unavailable. Ten months to January 2026 already contained ₹287.162 crore revenue and ₹21.5507 crore PAT; the final two months add ₹36.938 crore revenue but only ₹1.6163 crore PAT. That uneven profitability and late inventory accumulation argue against annualizing the strongest interim margin. No durable contracted order backlog is assumed.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: The opportunity is to convert processing capacity, sourcing diversity and new distribution into repeat sales without continually borrowing to carry inventory. FY26 inventory rises ₹41.2643 crore, vendor advances reach ₹30.1549 crore and customer advances ₹28.2561 crore finance part of the cycle. Net operating working capital is reconstructed from actual balances at ₹48.6244 crore, not backfilled from a sales ratio. Three-year incremental normalized NOPAT on equity-plus-debt capital is about 38.52%, and one-year about 36.49%, using 26% normalized tax; these are backward-looking and strongly depend on a low-margin/very small starting base and the processing transition. A constant early margin would yield far less. CAP 5 therefore does not adopt the headline return as a durable hurdle spread. Cash conversion overrides sales enthusiasm: GQS capped 5. Existing FY26 spending includes ₹3.0159 crore vehicle additions and ₹2.0291 crore investment-property purchases, not just productive processing equipment; no personal-use allegation follows from the asset classes.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: September 28 AGM record-date promoter category is 15,061,998/23,017,270 shares, 65.4378%; this corroborates the percentage on a dated basis, not a September 30 pledge clearance. The July 8 Patel-group acquisition is a non-promoter PAC holding change, not promoter buying. FY26 director remuneration ₹1.365 crore is 5.89% of PAT, versus ₹0.715 crore FY25; restated FY24 remuneration ₹2 crore exceeded that year’s ₹1.7897 crore PAT, so pay should be monitored through a cycle. AOC2 discloses connected Draps Ventures purchases ₹9.0315 crore, commission ₹0.495 crore and a relative’s professional fee ₹0.18 crore. January related-lender balances are not relabelled March balances. Financial/IFC opinions are unmodified and audit-trail reporting affirmative; broad confirmation language covers receivables, payables, borrowings, advances and deposits. The annual subsidiary statements conflict as described in the header; August approved Dubai liquidation and September actually incorporated Chile with USD 10,000 nominal capital. These are reporting/scope questions, not findings of diversion. IPO disclosures describe PF/ESI delays with corrective action; current universal compliance is not inferred. Statutory reaudit for IPO peer-review purposes and later internal/secretarial appointments are not assumed resignations over dispute.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text: Restated FY23/24/25 PAT ₹0.0859/₹1.7897/₹7.2210 crore differs from original reports ₹0.1291/₹1.9101/₹7.0868 crore; the original FY25 comparative also gives FY24₹1.9139 crore. The prospectus discloses depreciation, gratuity, tax, prepaid and expense adjustments; later series is used rather than spliced with originals. FY26 PAT ₹23.1670 crore contains ₹0.8211 crore other income, mostly ₹0.7524 crore FX gain. Removing all other income at 24–28% tax gives core PAT roughly ₹22.543–₹22.576 crore; recurring tax-interest costs ₹0.8611 crore are not casually added back. Reported weighted EPS ₹13.89 and separate bonus-adjusted note ₹14.08 are not post-IPO earning power: PAT/current 2.301727 crore shares=₹10.0651 illustrative per-share profit. Historical bonus/EPS bases are separately labeled. FY24–26 CFO totals −₹6.0267 crore versus PAT ₹32.1777 crore, −0.1873× conversion. FY26 CFO −₹9.0441 crore less PPE capex ₹5.1983 crore gives −₹14.2424 crore; after investment-property spending of ₹2.0291 crore, margin FD ₹6.4362 crore, deposits ₹0.575 crore and interest ₹2.1216 crore, economic cash absorption is much larger. MarginFD is not freely distributable cash merely because classified in investing. Actual unrestricted cash is ₹0.0702 crore, not total cash/bank balances of ₹6.5064 crore. January’s gross tax-paid line ₹7.5871 crore and provision inflow ₹6.3139 crore net to ₹1.2732 crore, while annual cashflow directly deducts ₹1.8018 crore; comparing gross lines alone would falsely imply falling cash tax. Current tax provision ₹7.9616 crore is reserved in the forward model.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: At secondary ₹96.70 and 2.301727 crore shares, market cap ₹222.5770 crore and reported post-IPO P/E 9.61×. That is not a current-cash enterprise-value quote: net IPO ₹38.4427 crore arrived after March, but its remaining October balance is unknown. The model starts from March unrestricted cash ₹0.0702 crore/debt ₹24.2838 crore, adds net IPO once, excludes restricted FD ₹6.4362 crore, deducts new office deposit ₹0.165 crore and illustrativeChilecapital ₹0.009 crore, and pays opening tax ₹7.9616 crore in year 1. No second ₹32 crore IPO working-capital deduction is layered on modeled WC. Base revenue growth 20/15/12/10/8%, EBITDA 9%, incremental WC30% of additional sales, maintenance ₹1.6 crore inflated 5%, incremental capex 8% of new sales,12% debt cost and 26% cash tax produce terminal ₹211.83 and 16.51% five-year IRR after 1% entry/exit friction and 0.5% annual dilution. Bull 35/25/20/15/12% growth,11% EBITDA,20% incremental WC and 15× exit NOPAT gives 36.45%. Base uses 12×, bear 8×; these are analyst assumptions, not claimed peer-certified multiples. Base remains funded without the conditional IDBI line; reserving an extra ₹10 crore of IPO funds reduces its return to 16.04%. Mechanical base hurdle prices 12/15/18% are ₹117.82/₹103.23/₹90.76, not limit orders or a margin-of-safety promise. R 6 reflects only 1.51 pp modeled spread above 15%, not the bull result.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: Severe stress assumes 30% first-year revenue decline,4.5% EBITDA,45 extra receivable days,20% opening inventory loss,10% receivable and vendor-advance loss,50% customer advance withdrawal, and ₹4.4445 crore customs cash exposure. The prospectus says DRI seized in-shell walnut imports under six bills of entry in December 2025 over alleged CIF undervaluation, with provisional release under court process against ₹1.7208 crore BG and pending adjudication; no show-cause notice was stated as of the reviewed filing date. Annual ₹3.4112 crore indirect-tax contingency, IPO ₹4.4445 crore maximum including penalties, and actual BG-related FD ₹3.9208 crore are different measures, not evidence of exoneration or a falling liability. The model is adverse sensitivity, not prediction of wrongdoing or conviction. It retains restricted FD outside free cash even while charging the full exposure, explicitly conservative if BG realization funds part of it. Debt service and core maintenance continue; discretionary growth capex stops on declining sales. Even with bounded ₹10 crore conditional IDBI headroom, maximum funding gap ₹45.27 crore; without the line ₹49.60 crore. Unfunded mechanical terminal price is not an investable IRR or liquidation appraisal. D 2 has Medium evidence confidence in the balance-sheet vulnerabilities, but high uncertainty in actual default/recovery outcomes.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: A low reported earnings multiple does not make fivefold or tenfold returns inevitable. At unchanged 12× normalized NOPAT and roughly 2.36 crore diluted year 5 shares, a 5× price near ₹483.50 requires about ₹95 crore operatingNOPAT before the cash/debt bridge;10× requires about ₹190 crore. Against normalized FY26 operating NOPAT of about ₹24.12 crore, that is roughly 32%/51% annual compounding for five years, with working-capital funding and stable margins. The actual base terminal ₹211.83 is about 2.19× entry price and bull ₹466.60 about 4.83× before friction, not 5× certainty. A brand premium, multiple rerating or release of restricted deposits is not used to fill the gap.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Require half-year cash flow with inventory ageing, vendor-advance receipts/settlement, customer-advance rollforward, tax-payment reconciliation and post-IPO use. Track actual IDBI draw, eligible warehouse collateral, annual renewal and expensive NBFC amortization: sanctioned capacity is not cash. Obtain dated customs adjudication status and distinguish an actual demand from a contingent estimate. Resolve the Dubai ownership/financial-scope wording and actual Chile funding. Require processing throughput and yield by product to correct the dates-utilization inconsistency; look for repeat-customer retention rather than customer-count growth alone. Secondary 60-session mean turnover bounds of ₹95.41–₹102.93 lakh/day and median ₹54.96–₹57.11 lakh/day imply 1.75–1.82 theoretical days at 5% participation, 4.38–4.55 at 2%, and 0.88–0.91 at 10%. These are low/high multiplied by volume bounds, not observed exchange turnover or executable depth. All 60 sessions have provider rows; none is zero-filled. The primary master lot of 2,000 costs ₹1.934 lakh. Current official MII decoding identifies SM as eligible and ST as dormant; the applicable ₹77.36–₹116.04 SM bounds represent a 20% band. Current BSE surveillance and queues are unverified, so L remains NS. Latest-day volume of 2,000 is just one lot, showing how the average can mislead. A dated secondary search discovery reports BSE Short-Term ASM Stage I as of 13 September; current status or removal is not verified. This specific unresolved ASM signal, rather than dormant master duplicates or absence of live spread alone, is the decisive reason for leaving L unscored. [SMASTERFORMAT] [SASM_DISCOVERY]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Speculative processing/trading expansion with a plausible valuation case but weak demonstrated cash conversion. The balance sheet improved with IPO equity, not retrospectively at March, and debt-funded working capital plus customer advances can reverse. Quality scores are rankable only with their Medium-confidence caveats; IAS is not rankable while L is NS. No order, allocation or public misconduct conclusion follows. Improve conviction only after cash conversion, collateral availability and regulatory exposure are evidenced; cheap headline P/E alone is insufficient.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Primary issuer annuals, original audits, final prospectus and relevant post-year filings were read; secondary OHLCV is explicitly not an exchange bhavcopy. Model histories and opening balances are factual disclosures. Growth, margins, incremental capital, exit multiples, stresses and FX translation of Chile capital are analyst assumptions. The five-year financial display includes a short FY2022 stub because incorporation was January 2022; no earlier history exists. Unknown current BSE restrictions, post-IPO cash use, latest pledges, subsidiary-scope reconciliation, unresolved customs case and fully harmonized EPS remain visible. Conditional models are complete but are not a contemporaneous audited October balance sheet. All source URLs and annual model rows are retained for reproduction; no ranking is derived from the undated CSV.

valuation.scope: Standalone AS, five annual forward steps from FY26 actuals plus documented IPO and subsequent-event bridge. Not a verified October balance sheet.

assumptions.cash: Net IPO proceeds of ₹38.4427 crore are added once after March. The ₹32 crore working-capital object is not deducted again outside modeled incremental working capital. Only ₹0.0702 crore of unrestricted March cash is included; ₹6.4362 crore of margin FDs is excluded from operating and terminal cash. Remaining IPO cash is not independently observed as of October; an additional ₹10 crore reservation sensitivity tests that uncertainty.
assumptions.working_capital: Actual opening operating working capital: inventory 41.7849 + receivables 20.5736 + vendor advances 30.1549 + government balances 2.8061 + prepaid expenses 0.1165 − payables 16.6074 − customer advances 28.2561 − other current liabilities 1.9481, all ₹ crore. TDS of ₹0.0145 crore is not free cash. Forecast net working capital is 30/20/40% of incremental revenue in base/bull/bear scenarios, an analyst assumption never applied backward to opening balances. No working-capital release is credited when bear revenue falls; customer-advance withdrawal is stressed separately.
assumptions.funding: Existing debt of ₹24.2838 crore is retained. Principal repayment is ₹4.4032 crore in year 1, then ₹5 crore annually, capped by remaining debt. Modeled blended interest is 12% in base/bull and 15% in bear, compared with disclosed NBFC rates of 12.5–17.15% and IDBI at 8.35%. The ₹10 crore IDBI sanction is conditional on eligible electronic warehouse receipts and annual renewal; it is not assumed already drawn. No refinancing beyond the explicit line or rescue capital is assumed. The opening current-tax provision of ₹7.9616 crore is settled in year 1 separately from future 26% cash tax; future tax accrual is not funding.
assumptions.operations: Base annual growth is 20/15/12/10/8% with 9% EBITDA margin; bull is 35/25/20/15/12% with 11%; bear is −30/0/3/5/5% with 4.5%. None is company guidance. Economic depreciation of ₹1.6 crore scales with the square root of revenue; maintenance capex starts at ₹1.6 crore and rises 5% annually; growth capex is 8% of incremental sales. Existing investment property is not added to terminal value at book value, and vehicle investment is not assumed to create a moat.
assumptions.subsequent: Incremental office rent is ₹0.33 crore in year 1, then ₹0.66 crore rising 5%; the ₹0.165 crore deposit is paid once. USD 10,000 of Chile capital is modeled at ₹0.009 crore using ₹90/USD, not an observed FX payment. No further Chile funding is forecast; expansion would require another sensitivity. Dubai winding-up cost is unknown, not declared economically risk-free.
assumptions.stress: The bear case charges 20% inventory loss, 10% receivable/vendor-advance loss, 45 extra receivable days, withdrawal of 50% of customer advances, and the prospectus maximum customs cash exposure of ₹4.4445 crore. This is an adverse scenario, not an expected default or verdict.
